title: Is embedding scale invariance the mechanism that defers compression?
design: Control arm tf_rms = canonical LN-free transformer + RMS-normalization on the embedding INPUT ONLY (per-token scale invariance; no mean-centering, no affine gain, no per-sublayer norm). It shares LayerNorm's scale invariance and nothing else. Compared against arms tf_lnfree (canonical), mlp, tf_ln (LayerNorm) from the same harness.
hypothesis: Embedding scale invariance is what lets the network reach correct predictions while the embedding is still high-rank, deferring compression to a later, norm-driven phase.

predictions.PD1_deferral: concentration completed by grok (frac-pre) < PD1_THR. Reference free-run values: canonical 0.75, LayerNorm 0.08.
predictions.PD2_norm_driven: post-grok Spearman(global_norm, embedding rank) < PD2_THR. Reference: canonical +0.70, LayerNorm -0.79.
predictions.PD3_fourier: top-k embedding DFT frequencies carry > PD3_THR of the power (the compression lands on Fourier modes).

acceptance_rule: The scale-invariance account is ACCEPTED iff PD1 AND PD2 both hold for the tf_rms control. PD3 is a descriptive check on what compression lands on, not part of the accept/reject rule.
note: PD2 holding is necessary but, as the run showed, NOT sufficient (tf_rms can show a negative post-grok norm-rank coupling without deferring); the accept rule is PD1 AND PD2, and PD1 is the discriminating prediction.
